citations.F1: `serialize_event` does one `SELECT ... FROM users` per event, so 1912 events = 1912 round trips — batch-fetch all actors in one `WHERE id = ANY($1)` query
citations.F2: Dedup uses `dedupe_key in seen` (list) → O(n²) over event count — switch `seen` to a `set`.
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` calls `requests.get()` synchronously inside an async handler, blocking the whole event loop ... fix by using an async HTTP client (httpx) or running it in a threadpool.
citations.F4: no index covers `(org_id, created_at)`, so Postgres does a full scan + sort of 4.2M rows for every call — add `CREATE INDEX events_org_created_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)`
citations.F5: `_request_timings` are module-level and never bounded or evicted ... cap `_request_timings` to a ring buffer (e.g. last N samples)
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` ... never bounded or evicted, growing for the life of the pod ... cap `_geo_cache` with a TTL/LRU
citations.F9: Don't ship the proposal as-is: more workers/pool won't fix a blocked event loop or the memory leak, and 16 workers × 50 pool × 6 pods = up to 4800 DB connections vs current 240 ... Redis caching just masks the slow path for 60s
